label: Claude Haiku 5.5
output:
Good evening o. Tolu, I'm Amaka, and I'm in Biology 100L now. I wanted Medicine too, so I know exactly how today feels for you. I cried in my cousin's room in Surulere for most of an afternoon when I saw Biology on the portal, and I didn't eat. I'm not telling you that to make you feel worse. I'm telling you because the first few days are the worst part, and then you start to see things more clearly.

I'll give you my own experience and what I actually know, so you can make a decision with the real picture.

**My story, quickly**

I scored 251 in JAMB 2025, applied for Medicine and Surgery, and got offered Biology at a federal university here in Lagos. My mum was telling people in church that I was doing Medicine for about two months, and I had to beg her to stop. Yes, that was embarrassing, but it also made me realise how much of that pressure was about other people and not about me.

**The transfer part, which is what you really want to know**

Transfer to MBBS after 100L is real. It is also not automatic, and anyone who tells you it's guaranteed or that it's impossible is guessing.

What our level adviser told us: you need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5, and there must be space in Medicine. Both conditions matter. Last year, about six people were moved into Medicine from the whole faculty, and she thinks over forty people applied. So the odds are not good, and I won't pretend they are.

On the CGPA, I'm at 4.31 after first semester. That is not 4.5. I'm still trying, and I might not get there. I'm telling you that because you deserve the real number, not a motivational one.

You will also need the Medicine cut-offs for your school, both the JAMB cut-off and the post-UTME cut-off. Your 268 alone doesn't tell them whether you're eligible. You will have to check both for your own school, because they change.

**What 100L is actually like**

Our courses in 100L are BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101, and GST. Physics and maths are the ones that deal with people. Some people in my class who had their hearts set on Medicine started failing those two and panicked. If you transfer, those grades are what you'll be looking at, so take them seriously from the first day.

Costs: my lab coat was 6,500 naira, the dissecting kit was 9,000, and the practical manual was extra. Budget for that before you commit, whatever you decide.

**Is Biology bad?**

No. I didn't expect to say this, but I'm enjoying it more than I thought I would. Genetics and cell biology have actually grabbed me. The first BIO practical we did was dissecting toads. One guy in my group fainted. I was fine. That was the day I realised I actually like this thing, and not just the idea of being called a doctor.

Be honest with yourself about that. I'm not saying you'll feel the same way. I'm saying you need to find out whether you like the subject or only the title.

**About Ifeoma**

My secondary school classmate Ifeoma turned down a Pharmacy offer to rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she is still at home. I'm not saying rewriting is wrong. If you're truly ready, and you've really thought about what went wrong and what you'll do differently, it can work. But you need to know what you're signing up for. Staying at home is not as easy as people make it sound. Your mates will be in school, and it can get very lonely and very hard to keep your head up.

**Kingsley and Favour**

Kingsley, I respect that you want to help, but transfer is not a myth. It's just hard, and most people won't get it. Favour, "just read hard" is true but too simple. Reading hard won't fix the space problem or a CGPA that's below 4.5 if the space isn't there.

**What I'd actually do if I were you**

1. **Check your deadline this week.** You said the acceptance fee deadline is about two weeks from the 6th, so don't leave it until the last day.
2. **Go to your faculty or department and ask the exact transfer rules for your own school.** Ask about the CGPA requirement, how many spaces there are, what the Medicine cut-offs are, and whether accepting admission affects your ability to rewrite JAMB. Get the answers from the people who decide, not from forums, including me. I'm giving you my experience, not the rules for your school.
3. **Ask yourself one hard question.** Do you want to be a doctor, or do you want to be a doctor because of what people will say? Sit with that for a bit. Your answer matters more than anyone else's.
4. **Don't decide while you're still crying.** I know that's easier said than done. Talk to someone you trust, even if it's just one person, and get the facts before you choose.

Tolu, whatever you choose, it is not the end of the world. You can accept Biology and still work your way toward Medicine, or you can rewrite if you're really ready and have a plan. Either choice can work out, and either can go badly if you rush it. Take your time with the facts, and you'll be fine.

If you have questions about 100L or about how the courses are going, ask me here. I'll tell you what I know.

— Amaka_Bio100
